## FAQs

#### Q: What do I do with the output files?

A: With `--uniprot`, search `jcast_uniprot_merged.fasta`: Swiss-Prot plus the new T1 and T1 alternative-terminus
isoforms. Otherwise, append `psq_T1.fasta` (and, if you want annotated alternative termini, `psq_T1_alt_cterm.fasta` /
`psq_T1_alt_nterm.fasta`) to either `psq_canonical.fasta` (if you used `-c`) or your existing Swiss-Prot canonical
database, and search that combined file in your MS pipeline. Lower-tier (T2/T4) and orphan outputs contain
frameshifted or truncated sequences and should be interpreted with caution.

#### Q: What files are required in the rMATS directory input?

A: JCAST reads an unaltered rMATS output folder: one file per splice type, named exactly `MXE.MATS.JC.txt`,
`SE.MATS.JC.txt`, `RI.MATS.JC.txt`, `A3SS.MATS.JC.txt` and `A5SS.MATS.JC.txt`. Only the files of the splice types
selected with `-s` must be there. With `-m`, the cutoff is fitted on every one of these files that is present.

#### Q: Can I use a GENCODE GTF?

A: Yes. JCAST reads GENCODE's `transcript_type` as `transcript_biotype`. When no transcript of a gene passes the
canonical filter, it uses the transcript GENCODE tags `Ensembl_canonical` (see the [Documentation](about.qmd)).

#### Q: Does JCAST write anything next to my GTF?

A: No. From v0.4.0, the parsed GTF is cached in the user cache directory, or in `--cache_dir`. `<gtf>.cached` files
written by earlier versions are no longer used and can be deleted.

#### Q: How can I contribute to JCAST?

A: Open an issue or a pull request on <https://github.com/ed-lau/jcast>, or contact us at
[edward.lau@cuanschutz.edu](mailto:edward.lau@cuanschutz.edu).
